environment.server: next start PINNED to 127.0.0.1 (-H), built from this tree

environment.productionDatabase: NOT touched: DATABASE_URL was pointed at the development cluster too, so not even the legacy pool could reach Supabase

howToReproduce: bash scripts/run-api-http-proof.sh    # allocates its own free ports and proof database, and creates its own cluster unless DEV_DB_PORT is set
# or, against a cluster you already run: DEV_DB_PORT=5501 bash scripts/run-api-http-proof.sh
resourceOwnership: the proof server ran on an OS-allocated free port, PINNED to 127.0.0.1, with a per-port database name, and the development cluster was created by THIS run in its own data directory under a run directory that carries this run's ownership marker (unless DEV_DB_PORT was supplied, in which case the caller's cluster was used and left running). Ownership is decided in ONE pid namespace: the tree this run starts is translated to its WINDOWS pid through the platform's own mapping (`ps -W`, whose WINPID column is the OS's own table) at start time, because Git Bash's `$!` counts in MSYS pids and a `$!` handed to `taskkill` would address an unrelated Windows process — and a listener that answered the readiness probe but is not in the started tree fails the run before any work is done on it. Cleanup stopped only the process TREE this run started — ownership is decided by process LINEAGE, never by the port number, so a foreign listener that won the race for the allocated port is reported and left running — checked the exit status of every stop, and VERIFIED termination before deleting anything. When termination could not be verified the run directory and the cluster data directory were PRESERVED and the failure was reported; `node scripts/dev-db.mjs destroy` refuses the same thing for the same reason. Termination and preservation are exercised by `bash scripts/run-http-proof-safety.sh`.

manifest.canonicalForm: one line per file, sorted by `path` (ascending byte order, `/` separators): "<sha256>  <bytes>  <path>\n" — two spaces as the separator, size in bytes as decimal, LF line endings, no trailing blank line — hashed with sha256
